title: Epic used AI to find potential security flaws that could expose patient health records
key_facts: Epic Systems, a Verona, Wisconsin electronic health records company, used Anthropic's Claude Mythos model to find security weaknesses that could give hackers undetectable access to patient data.
Chief executive Judy Faulkner revealed the flaws and the tool's use at a conference last month (September 2026), according to The New York Times.
Faulkner said Epic paused certain new product development to apply the patches the AI identified.
NYT reporter Christopher Rowland said the tool did not verify whether records could be changed, which he said would be of particular concern.
Epic controlled nearly 44% of the acute-care electronic health record market last year (KLAS Research); three firms hold nearly 75% (Definitive Healthcare).

University of Wisconsin-Eau Claire professor Rahul Gomes said AI speeds up both attack and defence, and that a shared platform is both an advantage for standard defences and a single point of weakness.
quote_evidence: Faulkner announced that Epic had paused certain new elements of product development to implement patches the AI agent identified.
While the AI tool did not verify if health records could be changed, he said the ability to do so is of particular concern.
Epic Systems controlled nearly 44 percent of the market for acute care electronic health records last year, according to KLAS Research.
why_it_matters_hint: The largest US health-record vendor says it used a frontier AI model to find flaws that could expose patient data, showing AI used for defence in healthcare, though details of the flaws are not given.
event_date: Faulkner's conference remarks in September 2026 (exact date not stated); WPR article 8 Oct 2026
notes: Older news re-reported: the revelation was made at a conference 'last month'; WPR relays The New York Times (original not opened). Score lowered by one for staleness. No details of the flaws, number affected or evidence of exploitation are given.
